# gitignore-excludes

Back up source trees with [restic](https://restic.net) or [borg](https://www.borgbackup.org) and
skip everything Git ignores (`node_modules`, virtualenvs, build output, caches). The tool asks Git
which paths are ignored in every working tree below a directory and writes them as an exclude file:

```console
$ gitignore-excludes ~/code > /tmp/code-excludes.txt
gitignore-excludes: 11 working trees, 27 ignored paths
$ restic backup ~/code --exclude-file /tmp/code-excludes.txt
```

```console
$ head -4 /tmp/code-excludes.txt
# generated by gitignore-excludes; regenerate before each backup
/home/me/code/api/.venv
/home/me/code/api/src/api/__pycache__
/home/me/code/web/node_modules
```

On the author's project folder with 11 repositories, the restic backup went from 4253 files /
86.6 MiB to 604 files / 1.1 MiB.

## Why

restic and borg have no option to read `.gitignore` files. Developers who back up their source
directories either back up every dependency and build tree or maintain exclude patterns by hand:

- [restic/restic#1514](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/1514) "Use .gitignore (or other VCS)
  for excluding files": 70 reactions, 27 comments, open since December 2017. In the thread, a
  restic contributor (now the author of rustic)
  [voted](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/1514#issuecomment-752224774) for "an easy way to
  use a suitable external tool" instead of building it into restic.
- [restic/restic#4227](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/4227), the pull request implementing
  it: 20 reactions, open since March 2023 with no review submitted.
- [borgbackup/borg#641](https://github.com/borgbackup/borg/issues/641) "read relative exclude paths
  from files within backup source": 24 reactions, open since 2016;
  [borg#937](https://github.com/borgbackup/borg/issues/937) "exclude files specified in .gitignore"
  was closed without a feature.
- Forum threads: [Gitignore style excludes](https://forum.restic.net/t/gitignore-style-excludes/1131),
  [Skipping git-ignored files](https://forum.restic.net/t/skipping-git-ignored-files/4638).

The workarounds posted there pipe `rg --files` or `fd` into `restic backup --files-from-verbatim`.
They match ignore files with a different implementation than Git's, and they make every listed file
a snapshot path, so the path list changes whenever a file is added or removed;
[restic#2246](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/2246) "Parent-snapshot detection fails with
changing --files-from" is still open. Another approach writes `CACHEDIR.TAG` files into ignored
directories, which modifies the working trees and cannot exclude single files.
[rustic](https://github.com/rustic-rs/rustic) and [kopia](https://kopia.io) can read ignore files,
but that means switching backup tools. GNU `tar` has `--exclude-vcs-ignores`.

gitignore-excludes keeps the backup tool and the backup paths as they are and adds one
`--exclude-file`.

## How it works

For each directory below ROOT that contains `.git`, it runs

```sh
git ls-files -z --others --ignored --exclude-standard --directory
```

so the result follows Git's own rules: nested `.gitignore` files, negation (`!keep.log`),
`.git/info/exclude` and `core.excludesFile`. Tracked files are never excluded, even when a pattern
matches them. A directory that is ignored as a whole becomes one line, and the walk does not
descend into it. Each path is written as an absolute, escaped pattern that matches only that path:

- restic: `*`, `?`, `[` and `\` are escaped with `\`, `$` becomes `$$` (restic expands environment
  variables in exclude files), trailing whitespace becomes `[ ]`.
- borg: `pp:/path` (literal path prefix); `fm:` with escaped characters for names that end in
  whitespace.

## Installation

Requires Python 3.10+ and git. No other dependencies.

```sh
pipx install git+https://github.com/Jwrede/gitignore-excludes
# or run without installing
uvx --from git+https://github.com/Jwrede/gitignore-excludes gitignore-excludes --help
```

## Usage

```
gitignore-excludes [-f restic|borg|plain] [-k GLOB]... [-o FILE] [-z] [-q] ROOT [ROOT ...]
```

- `-f restic` (default) for `restic backup --exclude-file FILE`.
- `-f borg` for `borg create --exclude-from FILE`.
- `-f plain` prints raw absolute paths, one per line (`-z`: NUL-separated).
- `-k GLOB` / `--keep GLOB` never excludes ignored entries whose name matches GLOB. An ignored
  directory that contains a kept file is not excluded as a whole; its other children are.
- `-o FILE` writes the file atomically instead of printing to stdout.
- A summary goes to stderr (`-q` to silence); repositories Git refuses to read (for example
  "dubious ownership") are reported as warnings and skipped.

Example backup script:

```sh
gitignore-excludes ~/code ~/work -k '.env*' -o ~/.cache/backup-excludes.txt
restic backup ~/code ~/work --exclude-file ~/.cache/backup-excludes.txt

gitignore-excludes ~/code -f borg -o ~/.cache/borg-excludes.txt
borg create --exclude-from ~/.cache/borg-excludes.txt /backup/repo::'{now}' ~/code
```

## Things to check before relying on it

- **Ignored files are often secrets.** `.env`, keystores and local config are usually in
  `.gitignore` because they must not be committed, and they may exist nowhere else. Run with
  `-f plain` once and read the list, then add `--keep` patterns for anything you need in the backup.
- Regenerate the file before every backup. The list contains concrete paths, so files that become
  ignored later are not excluded until the next run.
- Pass the same ROOT paths to the tool and the backup command. The patterns are absolute; with borg,
  back up absolute paths, since borg stores relative arguments as relative paths. Symlinks are not
  followed and are not resolved.
- Only Git working trees are handled. Directories outside a repository and other VCS ignore files
  (`.hgignore`) are left alone. A repository inside an ignored directory is excluded with it.
- File names containing a newline cannot be written into a line-based exclude file; the newline
  becomes `?`, which also matches other single characters at that position.
- Tested on Linux with restic 0.19.1 and borg 1.4.5 (CI runs both end to end, including file names
  with `*`, `?`, `[`, `\`, `$` and trailing spaces). Not tested on Windows or macOS.

## Development

```sh
pip install -e ".[dev]"
pytest -v
```

The end-to-end tests back up a fixture tree with restic and borg and compare the snapshot contents
with the files Git does not ignore. They are skipped when the binaries are not on `PATH`.
